install-angular-cli.metaTitle: Install Angular with npm: Node.js and CLI
install-angular-cli.description: Install Angular the right way: Node.js, then npm install -g @angular/cli. Check your versions, fix common errors and learn why npm install angular is different.

addFaqs.q: What is the command to install Angular?
addFaqs.a: Install Node.js first, then run npm install -g @angular/cli to install the Angular CLI. After that, ng new my-app creates a new Angular project. You do not install Angular on its own: the CLI sets up the project and its Angular packages for you.

addFaqs.q: Does npm install angular install the modern Angular framework?
addFaqs.a: No. The npm package named angular is the old AngularJS (version 1.x). Modern Angular is installed through the Angular CLI with npm install -g @angular/cli and ng new. If a tutorial tells you to run npm install angular, check that it is not about AngularJS.

addFaqs.q: Is AngularJS the same as Angular?
addFaqs.a: No. AngularJS is the first version (1.x) and its official support ended on 31 December 2021. Angular (version 2 and later) is a different, rewritten framework, and it is what this course teaches. Use Angular for new projects.

angular-project-structure.metaTitle: Angular Project Structure and App Flow
angular-project-structure.description: See how an Angular app starts: from index.html and main.ts to the root component, with a tour of app.config.ts, angular.json and the src folder.

addFaqs.q: How does an Angular app start and run?
addFaqs.a: The browser loads index.html, which holds the app-root tag and the compiled scripts. main.ts then calls bootstrapApplication with the root component and the settings from app.config.ts, and Angular draws that component inside app-root. From there the root component shows other components, and if the app uses routing, the router decides which page to display.
